scLimbsCoveredByACT: NONE. The ACT corpus for SC 4.1.3 is completely empty. The inventory (eval/act-augmented/_resources/4.1.3.json) reports actRuleCount:0, testCaseCount:0, testCaseCountsByExpected:{}, with empty actRules[] and testCases[] arrays. No ACT rule and no ACT test case (passed/failed/inapplicable) addresses any limb of this SC. Every limb below is absent because the WHOLE corpus is absent, not because of selective gaps. The only structured material that exists for this SC is 9 WCAG techniques (5 sufficient: ARIA19, ARIA22, ARIA23, ARIA25, ARIA27; 1 failure: F103; 1 general: G193; 2 advisory: ARIA18, SCR14) plus 25 hand-authored seed PATTERNS in eval/act-augmented/_seeds/by-sc/4.1.3.json. Neither techniques nor seeds are ACT rules/test cases.
scLimbsAbsentFromACT: Definitional limb A - the message 'provides information to the user on the success or results of an action, on the waiting state of an application, on the progress of a process, or on the existence of errors' (Understanding intent; F103 test step 2). All four information sub-types are absent from ACT: (a) success/result of an action ('5 results returned', 'Your form was successfully submitted', 'Saved in Wedding album', 'Add to cart -> 5 items'); (b) waiting state ('application busy', 'Searching...'); (c) progress of a process (dynamic progress bar, ARIA25/ARIA27); (d) existence of errors ('Invalid entry', '5 errors on page').

Definitional limb B - 'the message is not delivered via a change in context' / 'does not take focus' (Understanding intent; F103 test step 1). The change-of-context EXCLUSION boundary is entirely untested in ACT: no case for the in-scope side (status added without taking focus) and none for the three excepted cases the Understanding enumerates (error shown in a dialog that takes focus; expand/collapse of menu/select/accordion/tab state changes already governed by 4.1.2; new survey questions added that do not meet the status-message definition).

Core operative limb - the status message is 'programmatically determined through role or properties' (SC text; F103 step 3). No ACT case verifies presence/absence of any of F103's listed mechanisms: HTML <output>, role=status, role=alert, role=log, or aria-live=polite/assertive. The five sufficient techniques (ARIA19 alert/live region for errors, ARIA22 role=status, ARIA23 role=log, ARIA25/ARIA27 progressbar live region) map directly to this limb but have ZERO corresponding ACT rules/cases.

Failure limb (F103) - the full failure shape: dynamic content that meets the status-message definition but the container has NONE of role=status/alert/log or aria-live, OR the role/property is set AFTER the content is injected rather than before (F103: 'if the role or property is not set BEFORE the dynamic content is added, this also predicts a failure'). The before-vs-after timing limb and the empty-container-present-at-load requirement (ARIA19 test step 1) are absent.

Non-displayed-text-for-AT limb (Understanding 'Non-displayed text specific to AT users') - where visible text alone lacks the visual context, authors must add offscreen text to the status message. Entirely absent from ACT.

Modification-of-status-text limb (Understanding 'Modification of status text') - re-announcing the whole modified string (e.g. '0 items' -> '3 items'), correct use of aria-atomic so the AT reads the entire container (ARIA22/SCR14), and adding offscreen context like 'in shopping cart'. Absent from ACT.

Removal-of-status-text limb (Understanding 'Removal of status text') - where status text disappearing itself conveys status (busy/waiting -> available), needing a non-visible 'system available' message. Absent from ACT.
Non-textual status content limb (Understanding 'Non-textual status content') - status conveyed via icon or sound, surfaced through 1.1.1 text alternative + a status role. Absent from ACT.

Chattiness / appropriateness limb (Understanding 'Other uses of live regions' + intent 'doesn't unnecessarily interrupt') - polite vs assertive priority, and the advisory SCR14 ability to toggle/suppress non-emergency announcements. No ACT coverage of over-announcing or wrong politeness.

Scope-boundary note - the SC 'does not force authors to generate new status messages' (Understanding note); ACT has nothing distinguishing 'no status message present (N/A)' from 'status message present but not programmatically determinable (fail)'.

EN 301 549 C.9.4.1.3 - a pure WCAG-2.2 pass-through inspection ('does not fail SC 4.1.3'); adds no test material and inherits the empty ACT coverage. Trusted Tester does not cover this SC at all (trustedTester:null in the inventory).

Any 4.1.3 evaluation must rely on the dynamic LLM/AT lane, since the SC is inherently behavioral (content appears at runtime and must be ANNOUNCED) and cannot be judged from a single static DOM snapshot - exactly why ACT/axe have no rule here.

No positive (passed) examples and no failing (failed) examples: cannot calibrate either 'status message correctly given role=status/alert/log/aria-live/output' or 'status message present but no programmatic mechanism' (the F103 core). The four non-text/modification/removal Understanding sub-cases (offscreen AT-only text; aria-atomic modification re-announce; removal-implies-status needing a hidden 'available' message; icon/sound status via 1.1.1 + role) are the subtlest limbs and are entirely unrepresented.

Inapplicability/N-A handling - no case represents a page with NO status message (the SC must not force authors to add one); a detector has no negative-control fixture.

aspects.title: Live-region politeness is semantically wrong for the message's urgency and update frequency
aspects.description: The status message IS in a working, present live region and IS announced, so every automated tool and every seed (which all model the crude 'no live region at all' failure) passes it. The defect is that the chosen politeness is semantically wrong for what the message MEANS and how often it fires. Two opposite failure shapes: (a) a low-value, high-frequency message (a ticking stock/crypto price, a per-keystroke 'N results' count, a 'last saved 3s ago' autosave heartbeat, a 'people viewing this item: 14' badge) is wired role=alert / aria-live=assertive, so it rudely interrupts and clobbers whatever the screen reader was reading every few seconds, making the app intolerably 'chatty'; (b) conversely a genuinely time-critical / blocking message (session-expiry countdown, 'payment declined — do not navigate away', a security warning) is wired only aria-live=polite, so it is queued behind ongoing speech and the user acts before hearing it. Both politeness values are syntactically valid, so there is no markup error; judging the right priority requires understanding what the message means to the user and its cadence — a contextual call no checker can make from static markup.
aspects.scLimb: Chattiness / appropriateness — Understanding 'Other uses of live regions or alerts' + intent 'doesn't unnecessarily interrupt'; advisory SCR14 (toggle non-emergency alerts).
aspects.whyUncovered: ACT corpus is completely empty (actRuleCount:0, testCaseCount:0). All 25 seeds model only the binary 'message not in a live region -> silent' failure; none models a message that IS announced but at the WRONG priority. Automated tools (axe/WAVE/Lighthouse) cannot flag it because polite and assertive are both valid attribute values — correctness depends on the human meaning and update frequency of the message, which a static or single-snapshot scan has no way to weigh.

references.quote: to make users aware of important changes in content that are not given focus, and to do so in a way that doesn't unnecessarily interrupt their work

references.doc: Understanding 4.1.3 (Other uses of live regions or alerts)
references.quote: there is a risk of making an application too "chatty" for a screen reader user. User testing should be carried out to ensure the appropriate level of feedback is achieved
By default, when the stock price changes, the change is announced by screen readers. This could be annoying to some users, so there are buttons to allow users to toggle the announcements on or off.
The aria live region role of status has an implicit aria-live value of polite, which allows a user to be notified via AT (such as a screen reader) when status messages are added.

aspects.constructionStrategy: Each page mounts a present, valid live region at load (so the 'absence' checkers pass) and drives a real DOM mutation into it. Encode the meaning/cadence mismatch: either a trivial high-frequency value in assertive/role=alert, or a critical/blocking message in polite. Provide a sibling 'correct-priority' control region on the pass variants. Drive updates with setInterval / input events / timeouts so the harness can observe the cadence, and place verbose adjacent content the announcement would clobber or be queued behind.
suggestedScenarios: Search box where each keystroke updates a result-count region wired role=alert (assertive); typing 'shoes' fires 5 interrupting announcements that cut each other off — should have been polite.
Stock/crypto ticker in aria-live=assertive updating every 2 seconds, constantly interrupting the screen reader reading the article beside it (cf. SCR14's toggle-able polite expectation).

Session-timeout warning 'Your session expires in 30 seconds — click to stay signed in' placed in aria-live=polite so it is queued behind a long product description and announced too late to act on; should be assertive.
Autosave 'Saved'/'Saving…' heartbeat indicator in role=alert firing on every two-second debounce while the user types, drowning out their own typing echo.

A 'Payment declined — do not refresh' error injected into aria-live=polite while a verbose confirmation summary is still being read aloud, so the critical instruction is missed; an identical page with assertive is the pass case.
A live 'People viewing this item: 14' badge set to assertive, hammering the user with non-actionable interruptions every few seconds.

aspects.title: Partial update without aria-atomic announces only the changed fragment, losing meaning
aspects.description: A persistent status region is correctly marked (role=status / aria-live=polite) and DOES announce on change — passing every tool and every seed. But only an inner sub-node holding the volatile value is updated, and the region is not atomic, so the screen reader speaks just the bare changed token in isolation: 'three' instead of 'three items in cart', 'red' instead of 'filtered to red, 24 products', '2' instead of '2 errors on this page', '85' instead of '85 percent complete'. The visible string is perfectly meaningful because the sighted user sees the surrounding static label; the announced fragment is meaningless because the static context was not re-read. Catching this requires judging whether the spoken fragment alone conveys the same information as the visible whole — a semantic equivalence judgment.
aspects.scLimb: Modification of status text — Understanding 'Modification of status text' (re-announce the whole modified string; correct use of aria-atomic); ARIA22.
aspects.whyUncovered: No ACT case exists, and the seeds only cover regions that announce nothing at all — none covers a region that announces the wrong (truncated) thing. Automated tools cannot detect it: aria-atomic defaults differ by role and by AT, the page has valid markup with a present live region, and whether the announced fragment is intelligible on its own depends entirely on the human meaning of the surrounding (un-announced) label. There is no rule for 'announced text is grammatically/semantically incomplete'.

references.quote: where only the number in this string was coded as an updated chunk of content, the resulting experience for screen reader users could be to only hear "three", which may not be sufficient information to provide context for the user. In such situations, marking the entire "3 items" string as the status text would normally be a better solution

The role of status also has a default aria-atomic value of true, so that updates to the container marked with a role of status will result in the AT presenting the entire contents of the container to the user, including any author-defined labels

since role="status" is currently not treated as atomic by default in some environments, it is advisable to add an explicit aria-atomic="true" if the entire contents of the container should be announced

aspects.constructionStrategy: Mount a persistent status region with a static label + an inner value span (e.g. 'You have 0 items'). On the FAIL variant, mutate ONLY the inner span and either omit aria-atomic or set aria-atomic=false on a non-status live region (so the AT hears the bare token). On the PASS control, set aria-atomic=true (or rewrite the whole string) so the full sentence is re-announced. Trigger the update via a button/timer the harness can fire.
suggestedScenarios:
Cart status

You have 0 items

where only #count is swapped to 3 and aria-atomic is unset, so the SR announces a lone 'three'.
Filter result region 'Showing 24 products' where only the number node updates; SR hears '24' with no idea what 24 refers to.
Progress status 'Upload: 85% complete' where only the percentage span updates with aria-atomic=false, announcing just '85'.
Form error tally '2 errors found' where the count node alone updates and the SR says 'two' with no 'errors'.
Live 'Last saved at <time>10:42</time>' status where only the time updates, announcing a bare '10:42' that could be anything.
A 'Now playing: Track 4' status where only the track node updates, so the SR loses the 'Now playing' framing and just says 'Track 4'.

aspects.title: Role/aria-live added together with (or after) the content, instead of pre-existing empty
aspects.description: The FINAL DOM looks perfect: there is a <div role="status" aria-live="polite"> containing the message, with valid markup. A static scan and the seeds (which key on absence of role/aria-live) both pass it. But the region — or its role/aria-live attribute — was created/attached at the same moment the message text was injected, rather than existing as an empty container at page load. Most screen readers only announce mutations to live regions that were already present and registered, so a region born with its content never fires. F103 calls out this timing limb explicitly; ARIA19 requires the empty container at page load; ARIA22's test step 1 requires the role to be present BEFORE the message occurs. Confirming it requires reasoning about the ORDER of DOM operations (and ideally observing AT behavior), not the resting markup.
aspects.scLimb: Failure limb F103 'role or property not set before the dynamic content is added' / empty-container-present-at-load (ARIA19 step 1, ARIA22 step 1).
aspects.whyUncovered: Empty ACT corpus; the seeds detect the static absence of a live region, so a page whose final DOM HAS a correct live region sails through — yet it can still fail because the region was injected with its content. Automated single-snapshot tools see only the end state (a valid live region with text) and have no signal that the container was not present-and-empty at load; the failure is purely temporal/behavioral.

references.quote: Additionally, if the role or property is not set before the dynamic content is added, this also predicts a failure.
Check that the element containing the new content does not have a pre-existing aria role of status, alert, or log, or an aria-live attribute
The error container must be present in the DOM on page load for the error message to be spoken by most screen readers.
Check that the container destined to hold the status message has a role attribute with a value of status before the status message occurs.

aspects.constructionStrategy: Author JS so the live container and its message arrive in a single operation (createElement -> set role/aria-live -> set textContent -> appendChild, or innerHTML of a wrapper that includes the role attribute). The resting/inspected DOM after the action is a valid live region with text — so the page passes static analysis but fails behaviorally. Provide the PASS control where an empty role=status/aria-live container is in the markup at load and only textContent is written later. Note the timing in a hidden data attribute so the harness can distinguish.
suggestedScenarios:
Form whose JS does container.innerHTML = '
Saved!
' on submit — the role exists only after the text, so it never announces; final DOM looks correct.
Toast library that document.createElement('div'), sets aria-live=polite, sets textContent='Error', THEN appends — region and message arrive together.
Search page that sets the results wrapper's aria-live attribute via setAttribute at the same tick it writes the '5 results' string into it.
A cart status where the role=status attribute is added to an already-populated node only after the count changes, not on the empty node at load.
An error summary div that is display:none at load with NO role, and on submit gets both role=alert added AND the error list written in one operation.
A snackbar mounted into a freshly-created portal node carrying its message, vs. the pass version that mounts an empty persistent aria-live region at load and only writes text into it later.

aspects.title: Announced text lacks the visual context that makes it meaningful (no offscreen text for AT)
aspects.description: The status is announced cleanly and the whole atomic string is read — so tools and seeds pass. The failure is that the VISIBLE text relies on spatial/visual proximity for meaning, and no offscreen/extra text was added to the live region to supply that context to a non-sighted user. The Understanding's canonical example: a bare '3' appears next to a shopping-cart icon — sighted users understand 'cart: 3', AT users hear an orphaned '3'. Likewise a green checkmark + 'Done' next to a specific row, or 'Saved' with no album name where the visible popup sits over the 'Wedding' album. The remediation (add offscreen 'in shopping cart' / the album name, or place the icon's alt text inside the atomic region) is exactly the human judgment the SC's 'Non-displayed text specific to AT users' section calls for, and it cannot be derived from markup.
aspects.scLimb: Non-displayed text specific to AT users — Understanding 'Non-displayed text specific to AT users' + 'Modification of status text' (add offscreen context); ARIA22 shopping-cart example.
aspects.whyUncovered: Empty ACT corpus; the seeds only test missing/silent live regions, never a present-and-announcing region whose announced content is contextually impoverished. Automated tools cannot judge that '3' is insufficient without 'items in cart' — the text is non-empty, the region is valid, and inferring that the VISUAL layout supplied context the AT string lacks requires reasoning about meaning and spatial relationship, not parsing the DOM.

references.doc: Understanding 4.1.3 (Non-displayed text specific to AT users)
references.quote: the addition of visible text does not by itself convey sufficient information to the user of assistive technology. For example, the proximity of new content to other pieces of information on the screen may provide a visual context that is lacking in the text alone
In this case it would also be a courtesy to add offscreen text such as "in shopping cart" to the message.

Because it adds visual context, the shopping cart image — with succinct and accurate alt text — is also placed in the container. Due to the aria-atomic value, a screen reader will announce "Shopping cart, six items".

aspects.constructionStrategy: Build a layout where the visible meaning comes from an adjacent (non-announced) glyph, row position, column header, or overlapping label. The live region atomically announces only the volatile token (so it IS read in full — distinguishing this from the partial-atomic aspect) but the token is contextless out of its visual frame. PASS controls add offscreen text (visually-hidden span) or include the icon's alt text inside the atomic region. Make the visual context salient (icon, map cell, table column) so a vision pass confirms the gap.
suggestedScenarios: A live region next to a cart icon that updates to just '3' (no 'items'/'cart') after Add-to-Cart; visible context is the adjacent glyph the SR never reads.
A row-level status badge that injects 'Saved ✓' into a per-row live region but never says WHICH row/record was saved, while the visible position makes it obvious.
Photo-app toast 'Saved' announced atomically but omitting the album name the popup visually overlaps ('Saved in Wedding album' visually, just 'Saved' to AT).
A seat-map status that announces 'Selected' when a seat is clicked but not 'Seat 14C selected', relying on the visual map position.
A multi-step wizard status that updates to 'Complete' beside step 2's icon, announcing only 'Complete' with no 'Step 2: Shipping complete'.
A pricing table that injects 'Best value' into a live region near one column; AT hears 'Best value' with no idea which plan, since the column header is the only locator.

aspects.title: Removal/absence of status text conveys meaning, but nothing is announced when it disappears
aspects.description: A 'Loading…' / 'Busy' / 'Processing payment…' message is correctly placed in a live region and IS announced when it appears — so it passes the appearance-only test. The failure is on the OTHER edge: for sighted users the DISAPPEARANCE of that message signals 'now done / available', but for AT users the silent removal conveys nothing, and no replacement 'system available' / 'results ready' message is announced. The SC explicitly flags that absence can itself be status. Detecting this requires reasoning that the END of the waiting state is itself information the user needs — a temporal/semantic inference, not a markup check; tools never even observe the removal, let alone judge that it carried meaning.
aspects.scLimb: Removal of status text — Understanding 'Removal of status text' (absence itself conveys status; needs a non-visible 'system available' message).
aspects.whyUncovered: No ACT case; the seeds model only the additive direction ('message appears but isn't announced'). The removal-conveys-status case is entirely absent. Automated tools cannot catch it: removing a node from a polite region produces no announcement by design, the DOM after removal is clean, and inferring that 'busy text vanished, therefore the author owed a non-visible system-available message' demands understanding the workflow's meaning over time.

references.quote: In situations where status text is entirely removed, its absence may itself convey information about the status. The most obvious example of this is where a message is displayed that the system is "busy" or "waiting". For a sighted user, when this text disappears, it is normally an indication that the state is now available.

non-sighted users would be unaware of this change, unless the end of the waiting state results in a change of context for the user. Where updating the visible message (e.g., to "system available") is not feasible, the use of a non-visible status message, such as "system available", ensures equivalent status information is provided.

aspects.constructionStrategy: Author a busy/waiting message that appears in a live region (announced on entry) and is then simply removed (node deleted / display:none) once the async work completes, with the result rendered OUTSIDE any live region (or no completion message at all). The visible disappearance signals 'done' to sighted users; nothing is announced to AT. PASS control replaces the busy text with an explicit 'system available'/'results ready' string in the same live region. Use a timer or button-triggered fake async to drive the two-phase transition.
suggestedScenarios: A 'Searching…' spinner+text in a live region that is simply removed when results arrive; appearance announced, completion silent — no 'N results ready'.
A 'Saving your changes…' banner in aria-live=polite that disappears on success with no replacement 'Changes saved' announcement.
A disabled 'Submitting…' button state with a 'Please wait' status that vanishes when done; AT never hears the wait is over.
A chat 'Agent is typing…' indicator in a live region removed when the message posts, with the new message itself not in the log region — silence at the meaningful moment.
A checkout 'Processing payment…' status removed on success while the confirmation appears outside any live region, so AT hears neither the end of waiting nor the result.
An availability widget showing 'Checking availability…' that is cleared to reveal a now-enabled 'Book' button, with no 'Available — you can book' message for AT.

aspects.title: Non-textual status (icon/sound) given a status role but no usable text alternative
aspects.description: A status is conveyed purely by a non-text change — a spinner->checkmark icon swap, a red 'x' badge, a color/shape change, or an audio chime — and the author DID wrap it in a live region (role=status/alert), so the absence-of-role checkers and the seeds pass. The failure is that the icon carries empty/decorative/absent alt (alt='', aria-hidden, a CSS background image with no text, an SVG with no accessible name) or the sound has no visual+text equivalent, so the live region fires but announces nothing, or announces a filename, or announces a meaningless symbol. The SC routes this through 1.1.1: the role surfaces the change, but only a correct text alternative makes the change intelligible. Deciding that the icon IS a status indicator (not decoration) and that its alt misrepresents/omits the state is a semantic + visual judgment a checker cannot make — the markup is valid and a missing-alt linter cannot tell that this particular swap conveys status.
aspects.scLimb: Non-textual status content — Understanding 'Non-textual status content' (icon/sound surfaced via 1.1.1 text alternative + a status role).
aspects.whyUncovered: Empty ACT corpus; the seeds model only missing/silent live regions on textual messages, never a present live region whose status is carried by a non-text change with a missing/empty/wrong text alternative. Automated alt-text checkers cannot tell that a specific icon swap conveys status (vs. decoration), and a present role=status region with an alt='' icon is structurally valid; recognizing the state change is meaningful and the alternative fails to convey it requires visual + semantic reasoning.

references.quote: Where an icon or sound indicates a status message, this information will be surfaced by the screen reader through a combination of two things: 1) existing WCAG requirements governing text alternatives (under Success Criterion 1.1.1 Non-Text Content), and 2) the requirement of this current success criterion to supply an appropriate role.
Because it adds visual context, the shopping cart image — with succinct and accurate alt text — is also placed in the container.
After a user activates a process, an icon symbolizing 'busy' appears on the screen. The screen reader announces "application busy".

aspects.constructionStrategy: Inject a non-text status change (icon swap via /SVG/CSS background, color/shape change, or an aria-hidden glyph) into a present live region. On the FAIL variant give the icon empty/absent/wrong alt (alt='', aria-hidden=true, decorative SVG, or alt='icon24.png') so the region announces nothing meaningful. PASS control gives the icon accurate alt or co-locates an offscreen text label inside the atomic region. Make the icon visually unambiguous (red X = error, green check = success, spinner = busy) so a vision pass confirms the state is real and the announcement is empty.
suggestedScenarios: Form validation that swaps a gray dot to a red 'X' SVG (aria-hidden) inside a role=alert region on error; the region fires but announces nothing.
Upload widget where a spinner image (alt='') is replaced by a green-check image (alt='') in a role=status region on completion — AT hears silence at success.
Save button whose label gets a checkmark glyph via CSS ::after content inside aria-live=polite; no text equivalent, so nothing is announced.
A connection indicator that flips a CSS background-color dot from red to green in a live region with no text — color-only status with a present but empty live region.
A 'busy' state shown only by an animated spinner image with alt='spinner.gif' inside role=status, announcing the filename instead of 'application busy'.
A toast that plays a success chime and shows a checkmark icon with alt='' in role=alert; neither sound nor icon yields any announced text.

aspects.title: Mis-scoping the status-message boundary: change-of-context exceptions vs. genuine in-scope status
aspects.description: This aspect tests the threshold judgment that precedes every other limb: does the dynamic change even MEET the definition of a status message (success/result, waiting, progress, or error AND not delivered via a change of context)? Two failure directions, both requiring semantic judgment: (a) FALSE POSITIVE pressure — content that the Understanding explicitly EXCEPTS is treated as needing a live region or, worse, is force-fed into role=alert and over-announces: an error shown in a focus-taking dialog (already a change of context, governed elsewhere), expand/collapse of a menu/accordion/tab (governed by 4.1.2), or new survey questions added after a response (not a status by definition); and (b) FALSE NEGATIVE pressure — a genuine status (e.g. 'No results returned', 'Your form was successfully submitted') is left out of any live region because the author wrongly decided it was 'just content' like the search results list. The distinction between 'no status message present (N/A)' and 'status message present but not programmatically determinable (fail)' is itself uncovered. Tools cannot make this call: it is about whether the message MEANS success/waiting/progress/error and whether focus moved — pure human interpretation.
aspects.scLimb: Definitional limbs A & B + scope-boundary note — F103 steps 1-2 (does-it-take-focus / does-it-convey one of the four info types); Understanding 'Examples of changes that are not status messages' + 'not to force authors to generate new status messages'.
aspects.whyUncovered: Empty ACT corpus has nothing distinguishing 'no status message present (N/A)' from 'status message present but not programmatically determinable (fail)', and nothing modeling the three excepted change-of-context cases. The seeds only assume a status message exists and check for a live region. Automated tools cannot determine whether a content change meets the status-message definition (success/waiting/progress/error AND no change of context) or falls under an exception — that classification is the human judgment the whole SC pivots on.

aspects.constructionStrategy: Author pages that sit on the definitional boundary so the judge must classify before evaluating. For excepted cases (should NOT need a status role): an error shown in a real focus-taking dialog (role=dialog, focus moved) — N/A, and a version that over-announces it via an EXTRA role=alert is a chattiness FAIL; an accordion/tab whose 4.1.2 state change is correctly announced — N/A; survey questions appended after a response — N/A. For in-scope cases: a genuine 'No results returned'/'Form submitted successfully' left out of any live region (FAIL) vs. correctly in role=status (PASS). Move (or don't move) focus deliberately and label the intended classification in a hidden data attribute so the harness can score N/A vs pass vs fail.
suggestedScenarios: An error message rendered inside a modal dialog that takes focus on submit — excepted (change of context); the page is N/A even though no live region is present.
The same error ALSO duplicated into a role=alert region outside the focused dialog, so AT hears it twice — over-announcement of an already-surfaced change-of-context.
An accordion/tablist whose expand/collapse state is announced via aria-expanded (4.1.2) — author adds NO live region; correctly N/A, not a 4.1.3 failure.
A survey that appends new follow-up questions after an 'unhappy' answer with no status announcement — excepted by definition (not success/waiting/progress/error), so N/A.

A genuine 'No results returned' message rendered as a plain

with no live region — a real in-scope status that fails (vs. the same in role=status that passes).

A 'Your form was successfully submitted' confirmation added to the page without focus change and without a status role — in-scope success message that fails, distinguished from a results LIST (not a status) that needs nothing.

pages.scenario: E-commerce running-shoe store with an instant search filter: a 'N results' counter beneath the search box updates on every keystroke. The counter is a present, valid live region wired role=alert (assertive), so typing 'shoes' fires five assertive announcements in under a second, each interrupting and clobbering the last. A low-value, high-frequency count should be polite (role=status), not assertive.
pages.mechanism: role=alert maps to an assertive live region: each text change interrupts current speech. The region's text is replaced on every 'input' event, so a per-keystroke result count repeatedly preempts whatever the screen reader was reading and cuts off its own prior announcements. The message is announced (absence-checkers pass) but at a politeness inappropriate for its low value and high cadence — the 'too chatty' failure.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: A non-empty live region is present at load with role=alert + aria-atomic=true and genuinely announces. axe/WAVE/Lighthouse verify only that a status message CAN be announced; both assertive and polite are legal values, so no rule fires. No static or single-snapshot scan can weigh that a count firing on every keystroke is low-value, high-cadence content that should be polite — that needs human understanding of the message's meaning and frequency.

citation.doc: WCAG 2.2 Understanding SC 4.1.3 Status Messages — 'Other uses of live regions or alerts' (wcag-understanding/status-messages.html)
citation.quote: Live regions and alerts can be usefully applied in many situations where a change of content takes place which does not constitute a status message, as defined in this success criterion. However, there is a risk of making an application too "chatty" for a screen reader user. User testing should be carried out to ensure the appropriate level of feedback is achieved.

pages.scenario: Financial-news long-form article with a sticky 'Watchlist' price ticker in the right rail. The ticker is a present, valid live region wired aria-live=assertive, and a setInterval re-prices NDX/SPX/BTC every 2 seconds. For a screen-reader user reading the article, the price tape assertively interrupts the narration every two seconds, indefinitely. A ticking price board is the textbook low-value, high-frequency status SCR14 says should be polite and toggleable.
pages.mechanism: An aria-atomic=true assertive region re-priced every 2000ms re-announces the entire board on each tick, interrupting current speech each time. The user can never finish reading a paragraph because the AT keeps cutting in to recite fluctuating prices. The markup is valid; the defect is the wrong politeness for the message's value and cadence.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: The ticker is a genuine non-empty live region with a valid aria-live=assertive value and aria-atomic=true; it really announces. Tools confirm announcement is possible and stop — assertive is legal. No static or single-snapshot tool observes the 2-second mutation cadence or judges that a fluctuating price is non-essential content that must not interrupt; that depends on the meaning and frequency of the update.

By default, when the stock price changes, the change is announced by screen readers. This could be annoying to some users, so there are buttons to allow users to toggle the announcements on or off.

pages.scenario: Government unemployment-benefits wizard, 'certify your claim' step. The user must read a long legal certification statement before checking the agree box. A secure-session region (present, valid) is wired aria-live=polite; when the 30-second expiry countdown is injected, polite politeness queues it behind the long statement the screen reader is still narrating, so it is heard only after the session has already ended and the answers are discarded. A blocking, time-critical countdown must be assertive.
pages.mechanism: Polite live regions defer until the AT finishes current and queued speech. The session-expiry countdown is injected while four dense paragraphs of certification text are being narrated, so 'your session expires in 30 seconds' is not voiced until that minute-plus of speech finishes — long after the deadline has passed. The message IS announced (absence-checkers pass) but the politeness defeats its time-critical purpose; the correct value is assertive/role=alert.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: #sessionMsg is a present, non-empty live region with valid aria-live=polite + aria-atomic=true and announces correctly in isolation. Tools test only that a status message can be announced — polite is a legal value, so nothing fails. Determining that THIS message is time-critical and blocking (a session-expiry countdown), and is queued behind a long passage, is a contextual human judgment no static or single-snapshot scan can make.

citation.doc: WCAG 2.2 Understanding SC 4.1.3 Status Messages — Intent (wcag-understanding/status-messages.html)
citation.quote: The intent of this success criterion is to make users aware of important changes in content that are not given focus, and to do so in a way that doesn't unnecessarily interrupt their work.

pages.scenario: Higher-ed LMS essay editor with an autosave indicator in the toolbar. The indicator is a present, valid live region wired role=alert (assertive); a debounced handler flips it 'Saving…' -> 'All changes saved' roughly every two seconds while the student is still typing. Each flip assertively interrupts the screen reader's typing echo, so the student stops hearing their own words. An autosave confirmation is low-value and belongs in a polite region at most.
pages.mechanism: role=alert is assertive: each text change interrupts current speech. While the user composes, the AT echoes their typing; every ~2s the debounced autosave flips the assertive region twice ('Saving…' then 'All changes saved'), each flip preempting the typing echo (verified by MutationObserver capturing both transitions during active typing). The information is low-value, high-cadence — it should be polite (role=status). Valid markup, wrong politeness.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: #autosave is a present, non-empty live region with valid role=alert + aria-atomic=true (role=alert is even a sufficient technique). Tools confirm the message can be announced and find nothing wrong — assertive is legal. No static or single-snapshot scan detects that the region is rewritten every two seconds during active typing, nor weighs that an autosave confirmation is low-value content that should be polite; that needs understanding of meaning and cadence relative to the user's task.

pages.scenario: Coffee-store checkout. Submitting a declined card injects a critical, action-blocking instruction ('Payment declined — do NOT refresh or press Pay again, a second attempt may place a duplicate charge') into a present, valid live region wired aria-live=polite. On submit the screen reader is narrating a long order summary (line items, discount, shipping, tax, total, address, delivery note), so the polite decline is queued behind all of it; the non-visual user, hearing nothing, may refresh/resubmit and be double-charged before the warning is voiced. A blocking payment error must be assertive.
pages.mechanism: Polite live regions defer until current and queued speech finish. The decline instruction is injected while the verbose order summary is being narrated, so the 'do not refresh' warning is voiced too late to prevent the harmful action. The message IS announced (absence-checkers pass) but the politeness defeats its protective purpose; the correct value is assertive/role=alert.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: #payMsg is a present live region with valid aria-live=polite + aria-atomic=true; on decline it genuinely announces. Tools verify only that announcement is possible — polite is legal, so no rule fires. No static or single-snapshot tool can know this specific message is a critical, blocking instruction that must interrupt, nor that it is queued behind a long summary; weighing urgency against politeness is a human contextual judgment.

pages.scenario: PASS boundary: a bank sign-in verification screen with correct urgency-to-politeness mapping in BOTH directions. (A) A 60-second one-time-code expiry that BLOCKS sign-in is correctly wired role=alert (assertive) so the user hears the deadline in time. (B) A trivial 'Devices currently signed in: N' badge updating every few seconds is correctly wired aria-live=polite so it never interrupts, and carries an on/off toggle exactly as SCR14 prescribes for nonessential alerts. Politeness matches meaning and cadence, so the page passes.
pages.mechanism: Assertive on the blocking code-expiry warning is correct: it interrupts to deliver the time-critical deadline immediately. Polite on the low-value device-count badge is correct: updates queue behind speech and never preempt the user, and the SCR14 toggle flips aria-live to off so the user can suppress them. Both messages are announced, each at a politeness appropriate to its meaning and frequency — no defect.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: axe/WAVE/Lighthouse pass this page — but they would EQUALLY pass it if the politeness values were swapped (urgent message polite, trivial badge assertive), because both assertive and polite are legal and a live region is present either way. The tools cannot distinguish a correct urgency mapping from an incorrect one; only a human reviewer weighing each message's meaning and update frequency can confirm the mapping is right. This control proves the aspect is about human judgment, not markup validity.

A reviewer relying only on the quoted objective could mistakenly read SCR14 as endorsing the page's assertive markup.

The page conflates two distinct remedies in its narrative: the .md/HTML comments argue the fix is 'polite' politeness, while the cited SCR14 technique's remedy is a toggle (keep assertive but make it opt-out). Both are valid 4.1.3 cures, but the doc could be clearer that the defect is 'non-essential, interrupting status with neither reduced politeness nor an opt-out mechanism.'

pages.scenario: Coffee storefront header cart 'X items in cart' wrapped in role=status; clicking Add to cart rewrites ONLY the inner <span id=cart-count> 0->3 while the region has no aria-atomic, so AT announces a bare 'three' instead of 'three items in cart'.
pages.mechanism: role=status is polite and spec-atomic by default, but ARIA22 warns this default is not honored in some AT environments; with aria-atomic unset and only the inner count node mutated, AT speaks just the changed token ('three'), losing the static 'items in cart' framing that carries the meaning.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: axe/WAVE/Lighthouse see a valid role=status live region with good contrast and PASS it (they even credit the live region). They cannot determine aria-atomic's effective value across AT, do not fire the click, do not track that only an inner node mutates, and have no rule for 'the spoken fragment is semantically incomplete versus the visible whole'. Catching it needs a human to judge that 'three' alone is not equivalent to 'three items in cart'.

citation.doc: WCAG 2.2 Understanding 4.1.3 — Modification of status text
citation.quote: However, where only the number in this string was coded as an updated chunk of content, the resulting experience for screen reader users could be to only hear "three", which may not be sufficient information to provide context for the user. In such situations, marking the entire "3 items" string as the status text would normally be a better solution. See Sufficient Techniques for more discussion, including the use of aria-atomic.

pages.scenario: Hiking-boot faceted store with a result summary 'Showing 38 products' inside aria-live=polite; toggling a filter rewrites ONLY the inner <b id=count> numeral while the region is non-atomic (aria-atomic defaults to false for explicit aria-live), so AT announces a context-free '24'.
pages.mechanism: An element carrying an explicit aria-live (not role=status) has aria-atomic defaulting to false, so a non-atomic region announces only the mutated subtree; rewriting only #count makes AT speak the lone numeral '24' with no 'Showing ... products' label.
pages.whyAutomatedToolsMiss: A static scan finds a valid aria-live region, labelled checkbox facets, correct contrast, and real product markup — all green. problems: PROMPT/SCENARIO MISMATCH (metadata defect, not a page defect): the task prompt describes an entirely DIFFERENT case than what is on disk. Prompt claims an 'E-commerce running-shoe store' instant-search counter wired role=alert (assertive 'too chatty'), selector p#liveCount[role="alert"], cited against the Understanding 'too chatty' passage. The ACTUAL files are a 'Helmsley Workspace' notification-preferences page with a save-confirmation banner wired aria-live="off", selector span#savedMsg[aria-live="off"], cited against F103. The .md (lines 100-115) explicitly documents that the old role=alert scenario was REJECTED by a prior adversarial reviewer as advisory/non-normative and rewritten to the aria-live="off" F103 scenario. So the prompt is stale; I reviewed the file that actually exists.

The quoted SCR14 *objective* sentence does not by itself convey why this page FAILS; the actual basis for failure is SCR14's Test Procedure — 'Load the web page and verify that no non-emergency alerts are displayed' and 'Verify there is a mechanism to activate and deactivate the non-emergency interruptions' — both of which the page violates (alerts fire by default; no toggle exists). The page conflates two distinct remedies in its narrative: the .md/HTML comments argue the fix is 'polite' politeness, while the cited SCR14 technique's remedy is a toggle (keep assertive but make it opt-out).
